name: Executive order of May 4, 1886 adding the Paddy Cap extension to the Duck Valley Reservation
citation: Executive order of May 4, 1886 (Royce area 660; Kappler vol. 1, p. 866)
nations: Shoshone-Paiute Tribes of the Duck Valley Reservation (Paddy Cap's band of Northern Paiute)
promises: This was an executive order, not a treaty. It set apart Township 15 South, Ranges 1, 2 and 3 East of the Boise meridian in Idaho as an addition to the Duck Valley Reservation, for the Paddy Caps band of Paiutes and other Indians the Secretary of the Interior might settle there, except land already passed out of federal title or under valid homestead or pre-emption rights.
landTaken: None by this order: it added land (Royce area 660), less tracts already in private title or claimed.
today: No court, Commission or congressional finding about this order was located.

sources.title: Grover Cleveland, Executive Order Establishment of Duck Valley Reservation Extension (May 4, 1886)
sources.publisher: The American Presidency Project, UC Santa Barbara

sources.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule p. 920, executive order of May 4, 1886, Paiute (Paddy Cap's band)

openQuestions: How much land within the three townships was excepted as already in private title was not found.
